SOURCES OPENED: bible.md, the saal-bhar-draft-2026-10-26 review, ground-rules-draft-2026-10-25.md (owner answers 1 to 9 and the rules cited), personas.md, people.md, cutscenes.py, wides.py and portraits.py (styles, LOOKS, ROLE, WORLDS), the memory notes flux-portrait-biases and painter-glossary-rule, and the scratch notes method.md and realism.md, which hold the outside sources. The chapter facts come from the inventory's summary of chapter-1.json to chapter-5.json. Everything else is team judgement, marked as a proposal for the owner.

per_character.name: Nani (नानी), turning 80
problems: SILHOUETTE IN HER OWN CHAPTER. look.silhouette: 'A small seated triangle with the walking stick planted upright at her right like a flagpole'. That shape needs an armchair and a floor. Chapter 2 is her chapter and has the most panels, and there she is in a hospital bed and a steel wheelchair. The model sheet even puts the stick 'across her knees', where it reads as a bar, not a flagpole. Her best scenes are where she is hardest to read. Fix: add a ward rule to the sheet. In bed, the stick stands upright, hooked on the steel head rail at her side, handle at shoulder height. In the wheelchair it stands upright against the armrest. Then the upright line beside a small white head is hers in every room.

HER BACK ANCHOR IS HIDDEN BY HER USUAL POSE. hair: 'From behind she reads as a white line down a light shawl: her back-view anchor'. But she is 'almost always seated', and the chair faces the door, so her back is almost never seen. From the front she is 'a smooth white cap swept back', which is the same shape as Mummy's hair, also 'combed smoothly back from the forehead', no parting. Fix: when she is seated, bring the plait forward over one shoulder so it lies on the shawl and reads face-on. Keep it down her back only for standing back views.

HER ALBUM GESTURE IS GIVEN TO OTHERS. voice.tics: 'Counts heads aloud with her left forefinger'. This is the album's payoff ('And you.'). But Mummy's sheet makes it a standing pose ('THE ONE-FINGER COUNT ... exactly as Nani counts', pose 2), and Tinku 'counts heads behind Papa' in chapter 1. A shared signature gesture is no longer a signature. Fix: only Nani counts heads with a finger. Mummy counts things with her thumb, and the family likeness is shown once, in one marked panel.

WITH THE NAMES COVERED, HER WORDS COULD BE SOMEONE ELSE'S. uses: 'हिसाब (the accounts ...)' and the sample 'Haan. Aise. Hisaab poora.' sit beside Mummy's catchphrase 'Hisaab saaf.' and Tinku's 'Aaj raat hisaab mera.'. Her tic 'Opens with देखो when she instructs' is also Masterji's opening tic ('Dekhiye' / 'Dekho'). Her worry sample 'Fourteen people, ten berths. And Mausi's knee?' uses the same frame as Papa's 1.08 line 'Sixteen people, twelve berths.', and it also disagrees with his headcount. Fix: Nani owns the weighing words (तोल, पूरा, कम तोलना), Mummy owns हिसाब, and Nani drops देखो (her lines have no verbs anyway). Her worry names one person, never berth arithmetic: 'Badi ka ghutna? Neeche ki berth.'

THE TYPE TEST: SHE HAS BEEN SANDED INTO THE WISE STRONG NANI. never_does runs to 22 items, and most of them remove friction: 'never sets the women of the house against each other', 'never preaches', 'never complains of pain', never comic. Add the generosity in backstory ('tore up the credit book') and what is left on the page is a stock matriarch who is dry and always right. Her real faults sit in other people's files: Tinku says she cheats at carrom, and Captain sahab says she told him the 1979 umpire was right. No planned panel shows either. Fix: put one petty, visible fault in chapter 2. For example, from the bed she disputes Tinku's carrom score by voice note, or she overrules the nurse on how to read her BP. Then she is a person who can be wrong.

SOME PROP DISTINCTIONS ARE TOO SMALL TO SEE. prop: 'The T-handle keeps it apart from Mama ji's crook-handled umbrella'. In a 1024 by 768 panel shown at phone width, a standing figure is about 200 screen pixels tall (my estimate). At that size a stick handle is two or three pixels, so T against J is invisible. The purse's 'brass clasp of two little metal balls' carries plot at 2.21 and 2.22. Fix: tell the stick from the umbrella by posture: hers is planted vertical to the floor, his hangs from a forearm. Paint the purse beats as close-up inserts.

PAIRED WITH MAUSA JI, THE PROMPT INVITES SWAPS. across_looks says to 'write both people's top anchors into the prompt', but her fixed look is 105 words by my count. Two white-haired elders in shawls, each with a long text, in one prompt is exactly where the painter swaps traits (the method notes' point). Fix: in shared panels use her reference picture plus a short tag of about 20 words. Never stage the two side by side at one depth: one sits in front, the other is behind or in the doorway.

per_character.name: Mummy (मम्मी), 52
problems: FACE-ON, SHE LOSES HER ANCHOR. look.silhouette: 'a round bun at the back of the head with a thin pen sticking out at a slant'; hair: 'one big low round bun at the nape'. Owner answer 6 makes her face-on in chapter 3, her own chapter (across_looks 10). From the front a low bun disappears, and the head reads as a smooth dark cap, the same shape as Nani's. The square body is shared with Mausa ji. Fix: make the phone wedged on her shoulder her default stance (posture.stance: 'the phone is wedged between her left ear and shoulder'). A head tipped onto a raised shoulder reads face-on, in black and at phone size, and no one else has it, because Mama ji holds his phone up with a raised elbow. Or move the bun up to the crown so it shows above the head from the front.

HALF HER ANCHORS ARE TOO SMALL TO SEE. across_looks lists '(4) the man's wristwatch with a plain round white face on her LEFT wrist' and '(5) the key ring ... on her RIGHT forefinger', and gestures include 'THE KEY SPIN'. On a full figure at phone width, a watch face is roughly four screen pixels and a pen through the bun about one. A spin is movement, which a still picture cannot show. These are close-up props, not identity. Fix: save the watch and keys for inserts (winding the watch at nine, the keys at the shutter). Check full-figure picks only for stance, the dark block and the light diagonal.

THREE PEOPLE CLAIM THE DIAGONAL. colour_key: 'the darkest plain garment in her panel, crossed by one light diagonal band from the left shoulder to the right hip'. Mausa ji's signature is also 'one dark band of olive across the left shoulder breaking the square', on a square body like hers. Mami's is 'one thin strap slanting across her body'. The fix in the files, making Mummy and Mami mirror images, depends on left and right. The painter does not keep left and right, and a panel mirrored for layout swaps them. Fix: the broad light diagonal is Mummy's alone. Mami's bag goes on a short strap over one shoulder, which makes a vertical line, and Mausa ji's shawl is always wrapped round both shoulders.

HER ARC BEAT HAPPENS TWICE AT THE SAME TABLE. year_arc: 'In the front row beside Nani she sits back in her chair for the first time all year'. Mami's file gives Mami the same turn on the same night ('sits back in her chair, both for the first time all week'). Two people sitting back in one panel cancel each other out. Fix: sitting back stays Mummy's, because it pays off her vow never to sit behind a counter. Mami's release becomes something else (see Mami).

HER VOICE OVERLAPS WITH THREE OTHERS. voice.tics: 'Answers any question with a time or a price, feelings included'. Papa ('Every feeling he has comes out as a number'), Tinku ('answers with somebody else's score') and the player ('you turn every "and you?" into somebody else's news') dodge 'How are you?' the same way. 'Lists in threes ... Mud, stock, shutter.' and 'Paani kal tak. Maal parson tak. Shutter Shanivaar.' have the same rhythm as Captain sahab's 'Both lanes. One drain. Mended.'. 'Hisaab saaf.' borrows Nani's हिसाब. Fix: lead with what only she has: the phone greeting 'Haan ji, boliye', prices in rupees, and politeness that rises when she is cross. Keep the time-for-feelings dodge as hers, and take it away from Tinku and the player.

HER TYPING HABITS AND SAMPLES DISAGREE. typing.habits: 'all lowercase, no full stops, no question marks'. Yet her samples have full stops: 'ye 1840 ka. check karo', 'suno 8:45 tak ghar. daal tum', 'tinku 9 baj gaye. counter'. Her base style (lowercase, digits, thumbs-up only) is also Tinku's, and Mausa ji's only emoji is the same thumbs-up. Fix: give her one typed tell nobody else has, for example every message ends on a figure ('...counter 9'), and correct the samples to match.

THE RED PEN STOPS BEING SPECIAL. hair: 'a red ballpoint pen pushed through the bun'. The red pen is the player's one object ('your trace is the red of the red pen'), and Mami's file bans red pens for that reason. If Mummy wears a red pen in every panel, the one she holds out at 1.05 means nothing new. Fix: the pen in her bun is a plain blue or black ballpoint. Only the 'paid' pen is red.

SHE COPIES CAPTAIN SAHAB'S POSE IN HIS CHAPTER. year_arc, chapter 4: 'She stands at the back of the boundary with her arms folded'. Captain sahab's stance is 'At the boundary, arms folded high across his chest', and in Cricket she is 'dark cherry-brown' while he is cherry red. Same place, same pose, two reds. Fix: in chapter 4 she stands with her left palm flat on the scorer's table or on a post, which is her own gesture, and never folds her arms.

per_character.name: Papa (पापा), 56
problems: THE FIRST ASKER HAS THE WEAKEST HEAD IN THE CAST, AND A FALSE ANCHOR. face: 'Clean-shaven ... the only bare face among the five older men'. Masterji ('Clean-shaven every day') and Captain sahab ('Clean-shaven') are bare-faced too. 'ears that stand out a little' is written word for word for Masterji and Mausa ji as well. His hair, 'short black hair parted on his left and combed flat', is the most generic head in the cast. Faces drift, so nothing on his head will hold, and he is the first asker the player meets. Fix: exaggerate one head feature only he has, for example ears that plainly stick out (remove that phrase from Masterji and Mausa ji) or a tuft at the crown that never lies flat. Drop 'only bare face' from his avoid list.

HIS CHAPTER'S STYLE UNDOES HIS FIRST ANCHOR. across_looks: '(1) the tallest, thinnest line in the panel with the forward lean'. STYLE['lugdi'] in cutscenes.py ends with 'dramatic angle', and chapter 1 is painted in Lugdi. Low and high camera angles flatten relative height and hide a lean of 'a few degrees'. The player's file also bans steep angles, because they give the viewer a height. Fix: Lugdi panels with people use a level camera at eye height. Make the lean obvious (a man leaning into a wind), not 'a few degrees'. Whenever the coach roof is in frame, show him stooping under the upper berth, which says tall at any angle.

HE AND MAMI SHARE ONE SILHOUETTE. look.silhouette: 'a tall leaning line with a square at the chest'. Mami's is 'Bolt upright and tall, a flat rectangle against her chest'. They are height ranks 1 and 2, both have the 'line' base shape, both married in, and both are list-keepers. Their files even use the same voice measure ('Three of every four of his lines carry a figure' and 'Three of every four of her lines carry an ordinal'). Rigid against floppy and lean against plumb do not show at phone size. They share chapter 5 (her item 1 is 'Papa: trains') and the album. Fix: change the shape and the carry of his prop. His list is folded once lengthwise into a narrow slip, held down at his side or tapped against his thigh. The rectangle flat to the chest is Mami's alone.

THE CLEAR POCKET WILL PAINT AS NOTHING. prop: 'one sheet of plain blank ruled paper inside a clear plastic document pocket'. A transparent sleeve over a blank sheet in gouache or halftone paints as a plain sheet or a smear of shine. Fix: give the pocket a colour of its own, for example a pale blue tinted pocket with a darker edge strip, so the prop carries his sky blue.

HIS PATTERN DOES NOT SURVIVE THE SIZE OR THE PRINT. colour_key: 'pattern FINE VERTICAL LINES'. In Station it becomes 'fine enamel-blue vertical lines' under the style's 'coarse halftone dots', and the occasion kurta has 'fine self-coloured vertical stripes woven in'. Thin stripes on a figure about 200 screen pixels tall come out as a flat tint, and a self-coloured weave is invisible. Fix: use a few broad stripes, each about a pencil wide, in a contrasting colour, and carry them onto the wedding kurta.

HIS ROLE WORD BREAKS THE CAST'S OWN REASONING. role: 'Painter's role word: the father'. Mummy's file rejected 'the mother' because it 'might lead the painter to add a child to the panel'. Mausa ji's file rejected 'aunt' for the same reason. Fix: use a role word taken from his look or trade, for example 'the tall thin clerk'. It must not repeat ROLE's 'the man' (Ramesh) or 'the old man' (Bauji).

HIS TICS ARE SHARED. voice.tics: 'Says the number first, then the thing: Sixteen people, twelve berths.' Tinku's file has the same tic in the same words ('Says the number first, then the thing: Ten to pick from.'), and Mama ji's is 'Puts the number before the noun'. His typed signature 'Reached?' turns up in Mausi's sample ('Reached?? Khana khaya??'). Fix: Papa owns minutes, the 'X next' frame and the full stop. Number-first goes from Tinku and Mama ji. Mausi's after-trip message is about food only.

THE TYPE TEST: ON THE PAGE HE IS THE PUNCTUAL RAILWAY DAD. essence admits the type ('the punctual father with lists'). What lifts him, the boy waiting at the colony gate for a late goods train, is only in backstory. On the page he is corrections to the minute and 'Reached?', a family-chat stock figure. Fix: put the boy on the page once, without words. At the 2:10 am halt he stands in the coach doorway looking down the dark line, held a beat longer than the halt needs.

HIS HAND-OVER BREAKS THE BIBLE. year_arc 1.10: 'face in frame, the list held out in his left hand'. Bible line 78 says 'Household hands never reach towards you'. Mummy's 1.05 is already the one marked exception. Fix: Papa lays the list flat on the berth, turned to face the viewer, taps it twice and takes his hand away. That is rule-safe and gives him a giving gesture of his own.

per_character.name: Mama ji (मामा जी), 47
problems: HIS ARC LINE SOUNDS LIKE MUMMY. draft_fixes 5.27: 'Nine o'clock. Sixty plates.' | 'नौ बजे। साठ थालियाँ।'. That is Mummy's catchphrase frame ('Nau baje. Shutter up.' | 'नौ बजे। शटर ऊपर।') and her rewritten 3.26 ('Nau baje. ...'). Cover the names and the most important line of his year reads as his sister's. Fix: end his arc on his own tic, turned round. 'Pakka?' becomes a statement: 'Sixty plates. Pakka.' | 'साठ थालियाँ। पक्का।'. The worrier stops asking. Take 'pakka' out of the word lists of Mummy, Mausi and Masterji so it stays his (and Mausa ji's flat verdict).

IN JADUGAR, HE TURNS INTO THE POSTER'S MAGICIAN. across_looks: 'The magic-bill look turns a moustached man into the poster's magician ... the umbrella must not come back as a magician's cane or a wand'. A black stick with a J handle, on a moustached man, in a 1960s magic-show bill, is a magician's cane. ROLE already has Kader as 'the magician', and Jadugar is his only chapter. Fix: make the umbrella read as an umbrella in black. The canopy is fat and bunched under its strap, and the steel tip shows. It always hangs from his forearm and is never held by the handle (magicians hold canes in the hand). No composition in his panels echoes a stage.

HIS WEDDING CLOTHES LOSE HIS PATTERN AND COPY PAPA. outfits, WEDDING NIGHT: 'a sleeveless hip-length chocolate-brown jacket with a short upright collar ... woven in a fine tan check so his pattern survives'. A fine check is flat brown at phone size. The same cut, a kurta under a sleeveless stand-collar jacket, is Papa's occasion outfit ('a charcoal sleeveless jacket with a short stand-up collar'), so two men wear one shape on the same night. Fix: Mama ji keeps his large, hand-wide check on the wedding night, as a check jacket or a check kurta. Papa keeps the Masterji jacket.

HE SHARES A ROUND SHAPE WITH HIS SISTER. build: 'Round is held by a woman and a man, Mausi and him'. They are siblings at ranks 4 and 5, and both are in Nani's house in December and in the album. Two round figures of middle height side by side will merge. Fix: Mausi is wide and planted; he is round and always mid-stride with the raised elbow. Never paint him standing still next to her, except in his marked 'cross' and 'moved' beats.

HIS NUMBER TIC IS SHARED. voice.tics: 'Puts the number before the noun, as salesmen do: Seventy guests, sixty chairs, one tent.'. The same tic is Papa's and Tinku's. Fix: his only number habit is adding ten ('Sixty? Make it seventy!') with the flashed open hand. Counted lists belong to Mami in his chapter.

HIS SKIN CHANGE WAS MADE IN ONE FILE ONLY. skin: 'one step deeper than the cast map's warm light brown'. Mummy's and Mausi's files still call him 'warm light brown', and the change leaves Mami alone as the lightest person, the city in-law, which is the same colourism script his file set out to avoid. Fix: settle the whole family's skin on one painted swatch strip and update every file from it. Do not settle it in words.

TWO SMALL CLAIMS DO NOT HOLD. face: 'the only moustache among the speaking cast'. Mausa ji has 'a short white moustache that covers the upper lip', joined to his beard. Make it 'the only moustache without a beard'. typing: 'doubled marks (!! and ??)'. Mausi's typing also uses '??', and the player's file calls '??' Mausi's. Fix: '!!' is his and '??' is hers.

per_character.name: Tinku (टिंकू), 21
problems: HER CONTRADICTION IS THE PLAYER'S. want_fear_contradiction: 'Asked about herself ... she answers with somebody else's score'. The player's file says 'you turn every "and you?" into somebody else's news'. Chapter 4 puts them in the same scenes, and the player even names her habit ('Scorer, write your own score too.') while doing it themselves. Fix: Tinku keeps it, because it has a prop and a payoff (the blank back page). The player's contradiction is cut back to 'everyone calls you, nobody asks' (see You).

WITH THE NAMES COVERED, SHE AND CAPTAIN SAHAB SOUND ALIKE. samples: 'Three fielders. Pick fast, toss in ten.'. Captain sahab's 4.15 lead-in is 'Toss in ten minutes.', in the same chapter and at the same scorer's table. tics: 'Says the number first, then the thing' is Papa's tic word for word. uses lists 'bas', Nani's one-word closer. Fix: she speaks in scoreboard shorthand ('Three-nil', 'Nil for one', 'not out') with teasing tags ('haan?'). The toss call is only ever Captain sahab's. Drop 'bas'.

TWO OF HER THREE FACE FEATURES ARE OTHER PEOPLE'S. face: '(1) thick, straight, dark eyebrows, the mark of Nani's line' is shared with four faces. '(2) a small gap between her two front teeth' is also in Mausi's face ('a small gap between her two front teeth'). Her own file says the third, the eyebrow nick, 'may be dropped' by the painter. Fix: the tooth gap is Tinku's alone and Mausi loses it. The family brows should not count as anyone's personal feature.

HER COLOUR FIGHTS TWO OF HER LOOKS. colour_key: 'the teal must stay bluer than the outfield green, or she melts into it', and in Jadugar 'her teal sits close to the emerald highlights'. Nani is emerald in Jadugar, and in the album Tinku sits 'on the floor beside Nani's chair'. Fix: let the dark sleeves and black headphones carry her (a dark top edge over a mid-tone body) in every look. Move the body colour to a darker, bluer petrol blue that is neither outfield green nor emerald, and check it on the Jadugar strip next to Nani and Mami.

HER WALL AND CAPTAIN SAHAB'S CANNOT BE THE SAME WALL. painter_prompt: 'a plain whitewashed wall above it'. Captain sahab's file says 'His white hat would vanish into the whitewashed wall ... he stands against grey concrete or a mid-grey wall'. They share 4.06 and 4.15. Fix: their shared panels use one mid-grey plastered wall, against which both her white shoes and his white hat read.

THE SCOREBOOK IS THE GAME'S PICK COLOUR. prop: 'a plain ochre cloth cover', and her owner question 4 flags it. In every chapter 4 panel the asker would hold a block of the yellow that the UI uses to mean 'chosen' (rule 38). Fix: give it a dark cloth cover with a pale page edge. The wide landscape shape is the anchor, not the colour.

HER HEIGHT DIFFERENCE IS TOO SMALL TO PAINT. build: 'a little taller than Mummy' (ranks 6 and 7), yet 'Tinku grew taller than her at fifteen' is a story point. The painter will not hold 'a little'. Fix: make it a clear half head if it is to show, or drop it.

THE TYPE TEST: FROM THE NECK UP SHE IS THE STOCK GAME TEENAGER. Headphones round the neck, a plain raglan T-shirt and a high ponytail are the default young person in any game. What is hers alone is the posture with the book: 'knees drawn up on a plastic chair, feet on its front edge, the scorebook on her knees'. Fix: make that seated pose the front image of her model sheet and the default in her chapter, so the shape a reader remembers is the scorer, not a ponytail.

per_character.name: Mausi (मौसी), about 55, chapter 1 voice
problems: A SAMPLE LINE USES A FILM TITLE. samples, COMFORTING: 'Arre, arre, arre. Main hoon na. Aao, baitho.'. Mama ji's file and the player's file both ban 'Main hoon na' as a famous film title (rule 3). The next obvious swap, 'Main yahin hoon', is Nani's comfort line. Fix: 'Arre, arre, arre. Aao, baitho. Pehle khao.', which uses her own food habit.

HER TYPING BORROWS PAPA'S SIGNATURE. typing sample: 'Reached?? Khana khaya?? Kya kya khaya??'. 'Reached?' is Papa's one-word signature, and his file says it means 'I missed you'. Her '??' is also Mama ji's doubled mark. Fix: her after-trip message is about food only ('Khana khaya?? Kya kya??'). Her four-dot separators and voice notes are her marks, and '??' stays hers, not his.

HER WEDDING SARI DROPS HER PATTERN INTO THE STAGE'S COLOUR. outfits, OCCASION: 'a magenta silk-look sari with a broad old-gold border'. Her two-ink anchor is 'light ground, big dark flowers', and Nani's file names magenta as one of 'the stage's colours' in Jadugar. A plain magenta sari loses the flowers and sinks into the set. Fix: the wedding sari keeps the cream ground with big magenta flowers, in a silk-look cloth with the gold border.

SHE SHARES TWO OF HER THREE FACE FEATURES. face: the three things to remember are 'the open mouth with the gap, the copper puff, the hoops', and the tooth gap is also Tinku's. The hoops are 'thin', which is a hairline at phone size. Fix: give the gap to Tinku. Make the hoops thick enough to read as two bright rings beside the jaw. The puff and the open mouth are her strongest anchors; lead with them.

THE TYPE TEST: HER TEACHING IS INVISIBLE IN HER ONLY CHAPTER. The never list bars 'maths, coaching, teaches' until after D7, so 'in chapter 1 her teaching life shows in her manner, never in those words', and her Class 3 joke waits on Q5. Without it she is the stock loud aunty who feeds. Fix: show it with no words. She marks a pile of blank exercise books on her lower berth by lamp light, red-pencil ticks painted as plain strokes, as the bay settles. It is a teacher in one picture with no note word.

HER ROLE WORD BREAKS THE CAST'S OWN REASONING. role: 'Painter's role word: the aunt'. Mausa ji's file rejected 'aunt' because it 'can paint a second person', and Mummy's rejected 'the mother' for the same reason. Fix: use a role word from her look, for example 'the copper-haired woman'.

HER CATCHPHRASE WORD IS EVERYONE'S. catchphrases: 'Suno, suno, suno!'. Mummy's address word for Papa is 'Suno', Tinku calls you 'oye' and 'suno', and Mausi herself calls Mausa ji 'suno ji'. Fix: the tripled 'Suno' is hers. Mummy opens with the time to Papa (as Papa's file already has him do to her), and Tinku keeps 'oye'.

per_character.name: Mausa ji (मौसा जी), about 58, chapter 2's voice
problems: IN TWO INKS HE IS PAPA AND MASTERJI. colour_key: 'a plain, unpatterned mid-light shirt (dove grey) worn out over dark trousers (navy)'. That is Papa's light shirt over dark trousers and Masterji's lavender over black. All three are proposed for chapter 3's Station look, where 'value and shape carry him': Papa at the parcel office, Masterji as the voice, Mausa ji at the switchboard. Fix: wear the olive shawl wrapped round both shoulders in every look, day and night. That gives him a dark upper half no other man has and drops the band (see the next point).

HIS TOP ANCHOR IS OPTIONAL IN EVERY PROMPT. painter_prompt: 'SCENE ADDITIONS, one of: his thin plain olive-green cotton shawl folded lengthwise...'. across_looks lists the shawl as anchor 6, but it sits outside the fixed look, so the first panel prompt that forgets it paints Papa's twin. Fix: put the shawl, wrapped, into the fixed look, and let only the wool or cotton change by month.

A THIRD CLAIM TO THE DIAGONAL. silhouette: 'one dark band of olive across the left shoulder breaking the square'. Mummy, the other square body, owns 'one light diagonal band' over the same shoulder, and Mami a thin strap. In Rukavat his file paints him 'deep teak brown' and hers 'deep teak brown with a cream band', and Mummy appears at the ward door at dawn while he is on the bench. Fix: the wrapped shawl, as above, plus never painting him and Mummy in one Rukavat panel.

IN HIS OWN CHAPTER HE IS ONE COLOUR. colour_key, RUKAVAT: 'shirt warm teak-grey, shawl deep teak brown, trousers dark teak'. Every garment is teak, and the 'one signal orange' is a fruit in one dawn panel. Fix: carry him by the white brush-cut and beard (left as cream) over a dark teak block, against the pale cream ward wall that Nani's file already asks for. Do not lean on colour.

TRAITS DUPLICATED FROM OTHER FILES. face: 'ears that stand out a little' (Papa and Masterji too). gestures: 'THE CHECK ... taps it twice with his right forefinger' (Papa's 'TWO TAPS ON THE LIST', Tinku's 'Taps the pencil twice'). outfits, DECEMBER: 'a plain navy sleeveless knitted sweater' (Papa's and Masterji's winter is a charcoal sleeveless V-neck over a light shirt). Fix: his check is one knock of a knuckle, a lineman's rap; his ears are ordinary; in December he wears the olive wool shawl and no sweater.
WRONG COACH. outfits, NIGHT: 'the AC coach and the ward (chapters 1 and 2)'. Mausi's file dropped 'AC' because coach S4 is a sleeper. Fix: 'the sleeper coach'.

HIS ARC EXISTS ONLY IF TWO PANELS EXIST. year_arc: the dead bulb, 'The chapter's ending panel (1.40) can paint that unlit bulb above the wet step (proposal)', and the new lit bulb when Nani comes home. Nobody speaks it, so without both pictures he is the stock silent fixer uncle with no change. Fix: make the pair required, not proposed. Paint the bulb big in frame both times, from the same angle, so a reader compares them without help.

NOTHING SHOULD LEAVE THE FRAME TOWARDS THE VIEWER. year_arc, December: 'He hands you the other end of a stack of chairs: it leaves the panel at the bottom edge, where you are'. A load running out of the bottom edge is exactly where the painter adds the hand holding it (rule 7). Fix: he sets the chairs down at the frame's foot, turned towards the viewer, and steps back. The half orange is set on the bench beside 'you', not held out, which also leaves the held-out hand to the marked beats.

per_character.name: Masterji (मास्टरजी), about 60, the tailor next door; chapter 3's voice
problems: IN HIS OWN TWO-INK CHAPTER HE HAS PAPA'S AND MAUSA JI'S VALUE STACK. colour_key: 'lavender (light, plain) over black (dark)', and in Station 'shirt left as the cream paper, plain; trousers solid black'. Papa and Mausa ji are cream over dark in the same chapter. Fix: give him a dark sleeveless waistcoat, the one he cut with his 1988 jacket, over the lavender shirt, with the tape over it. A dark V with light sleeves is a shape no other man has, and it is the tailor at a glance. Then take the winter sleeveless sweaters away from Papa and Mausa ji.

HIS TAPE DISAPPEARS IN COLOUR. prop: 'a plain faded ochre band' worn on 'a plain lavender ... shirt'. Light ochre on light lavender has almost no contrast, and the tape is anchor 4. Fix: the dark waistcoat behind it makes the tape read light on dark in every look. Without the waistcoat, darken the tape.

EARS AND SWEATER ARE IN THREE FILES. face: 'ears that stand out a little under the bald crown' (also Papa and Mausa ji). outfits, WINTER: 'a charcoal grey sleeveless V-neck sweater over the lavender shirt' (Papa's is the same). Fix: flat ears for him, and the waistcoat replaces the sweater.

A TAPE RUNNING OUT OF FRAME WILL GROW A HAND. model_sheet: 'the tape off his neck, stretched across a crack, its far end running out of the bottom of the frame'. A taut tape leaving the bottom edge implies someone holds it, and the painter will paint that hand (rule 7). Fix: the tape lies slack across the crack with its end weighted by a brick or his shears, and he reads it crouching.

WORDS SHARED WITH OTHERS. uses: 'pakka | पक्का' (Mama ji's catchphrase, Mausa ji's praise). His opening tic 'Dekhiye / Dekho' is also Nani's 'देखो'. Fix: drop 'pakka'. Keep 'Dekhiye'; Nani drops देखो.

THE TYPE TEST: HIS FEAR IS ONLY IN BACKSTORY. The essence passes, since his digressive voice is the most individual in the cast, but what makes him more than the slow, late tailor ('In January a ready-made clothes shop opened at the far end of the station road') is never pictured. Fix: in 3.02 or 3.28, paint the new shop's bright plain shutter small at the far end of the road. It carries no letters or brand. His fear is then in the frame while he talks mud.

HIS VOICE NEEDS ROOM. voice.register: 'a verdict, then a wander ... when he has two bubbles, the second wanders'. The wander is what passes the covered-names test, but under the 10-word spoken cap (rule 62, waiting on Q14) and chapter word budgets, each of his digressions costs two bubbles. Fix: budget his lines as pairs from the start, and cut other chapter 3 words rather than his wander.

per_character.name: Captain sahab (कप्तान साहब), about 65
problems: WITH THE HAT OFF HE IS MAUSA JI WITHOUT A BEARD. hair: 'Close-cropped white hair, short as felt ... With the hat off, a flat-topped head under an even white crop'. Mausa ji's is 'Thick white hair cut very short so it stands straight up all over and is flat across the top'. His sheet takes the hat off twice: 'LAUGHING ... The one time the hat comes off' and 'OCCASION ... hat off, head bare'. Fix: the hat never comes off on the page. Laughing, he slaps his thigh with his left palm instead. Drop the occasion hat-off variant, so the head is the hat in every picture.

HE AND MUMMY TAKE THE SAME POSE IN CHAPTER 4. posture.stance: 'At the boundary, arms folded high across his chest'. Mummy's chapter 4 is 'She stands at the back of the boundary with her arms folded', in 'dark cherry-brown' against his cherry red. Fix: his folded arms are only for the umpire's spot in the centre. At the boundary he is side-on with the ball, and Mummy gets her flat-palm gesture.

HIS TIME TICS ARE SHARED. voice.tics: 'Rounds every time to the hour, the half hour or ten minutes', which is Mummy's 'Rounds every time to the hour by her fast watch'. 'Clipped triplets with no verb' have the rhythm of Mummy's lists, and Tinku's sample 'toss in ten' is his 4.15 line. Fix: his grammar is umpire's calls (Out, Not out, No ball, Wait, Over); drop the rounding tic. 'Nine means nine' survives only as his answer to Papa. Only he calls the toss.

THE BALL IS AN ANCHOR ONLY IN THE AIR. prop: 'held away from his chest so it never sinks into the red polo', with 'one half worn smooth and pale pink'. At about 200 screen pixels a figure, a cricket ball is a dot and its two halves are invisible. Fix: the front image of his sheet, and the default in his panels, is the ball in the air a hand above his open right hand. The toss is the silhouette, not the leather.

HIS TURN HAPPENS OFF PANEL. year_arc: 'after the last pick, on Sunday, he speaks off the panel over the mended drain ... That book. Show the district.'. This is his one change and the end of his stock-type grudge ('the strict old cricket uncle'), but the reader does not see his face when he gives in. Fix: keep the people-free drain for the outcome painting. Give 'That book. Show the district.' its own panel: face-on, side-on stance, ball held still, looking at Tinku and not at the viewer.

WALL CONFLICT WITH TINKU. across_looks: his white hat needs 'grey concrete or a mid-grey wall', while Tinku's prompt sets 'a plain whitewashed wall'. They share 4.06 and 4.15. Fix: one mid-grey wall for every panel they share.

ROLE WORD NEAR AN OLD ONE. role: 'the old cricketer', beside ROLE's 'the young cricketer' (Rani, 1992) in cutscenes.py. His file already notes that 'cricketer' pulls in kit and 1980s gear. Fix: use a role word from his look, for example 'the old man in the white sun hat'. That says the anchor every time it is written.

per_character.name: Mami (मामी), about 45
problems: SHE AND PAPA SHARE ONE SILHOUETTE. look.silhouette: 'Bolt upright and tall, a flat rectangle against her chest'. Papa's is 'a tall leaning line with a square at the chest'. They are ranks 1 and 2, both have the 'line' base shape, and both are list-keepers ('the other list-keeper', her own file says). The proposed separators, 'rigid ... and shows a clip' and plumb against lean, do not show at phone size. Fix: her clipboard is carried in the writing position, braced on her left forearm, tilted out, pen moving, and Papa's list leaves his chest (see Papa).

HER KEY COLOUR IS HER CHAPTER'S SKY. colour_key: 'the risk is that her indigo sinks into Jadugar's indigo night sky, so she is always lamp-lit and always painted against the warm canopy ... never against the night sky'. A character who needs a staging rule in every panel to be seen will be lost in the night panels (the gate at night, the eleven o'clock trunk). Papa's Jadugar jacket is also 'indigo-black'. Fix: turn her round. A pale kurta with the small indigo diamond print over indigo trousers reads against the night and the canopy alike. Check it on the Jadugar strip.

HER ARC BEAT DUPLICATES MUMMY'S AT THE SAME TABLE. year_arc: 'Mami sets the clipboard face down on the table and sits back in her chair, both for the first time all week'. Mummy 'sits back in her chair for the first time all year' on the same night beside Nani. Fix: Mami keeps the clipboard face down and drops sitting back. Her own release is to hand her steel pen to Tinku, who writes the last line, or to let Mama ji carry the clipboard away.

HER TIC IS THE PLAYER'S TEMPER LINE, IN HER OWN CHAPTER. voice.tics: 'Raises the pen, point up, for Ek minute. | एक मिनट। when someone talks over her'. The player's one temper line, in chapter 5, is 'Ek minute! Ek-ek karke, sab.'. Fix: the player's line drops 'Ek minute' (see You).

HER WEDDING SARI DROPS HER PATTERN. outfits, OCCASION: 'a deep indigo silk-look sari with a thin white edge'. It is plain indigo, at night, on the night of her climax (5.28). Fix: the diamond print carries onto the sari at the same scale, and if her base turns pale (above), so does the sari.

THE DIAGONAL STRAP. look: 'a small flat stone-grey canvas bag on one long thin strap worn across her body from her right shoulder to her left hip'. This is the third chest diagonal in the cast, separated from Mummy's only by mirroring, which the painter does not keep. Fix: the bag hangs from a short strap on one shoulder, a vertical line at her side.

THE TYPE TEST: THE PLANNER WHO CRIES AT THE UNPLANNED THING IS A KNOWN TROPE, AND HER REASON IS OFF THE PAGE. backstory: 'she spent her own wedding week not knowing where anything was kept ... she has kept a list for every family job since, on the same clipboard'. Only a joke waiting on Q5 says it. Fix: show it in one wordless panel. Behind list 24 on the clipboard is an old, soft, yellowed list from 2001, painted blank, and she smooths it once before writing. Her lists then come from that wedding week, not from being a type.

per_character.name: You (the player, a voice only)
problems: YOUR CONTRADICTION DUPLICATES TINKU'S. want_fear_contradiction: 'you turn every "and you?" into somebody else's news'. Tinku's is 'Asked about herself ... she answers with somebody else's score', in your shared chapter. Fix: drop the deflection tic. Keep 'everyone calls you, but nobody asks how you are'. The album still lands, because nobody asks, not because you dodge.

YOUR TEMPER LINE IS MAMI'S TIC, IN MAMI'S CHAPTER. samples: 'Ek minute! Ek-ek karke, sab.' | 'One minute! One at a time, everyone.'. Mami's tic is 'Ek minute.' with a raised pen, in the same week. Fix: 'Ek-ek karke! Sab, ek-ek karke.' | 'One at a time! Everyone, one at a time.'

FOUR HAND-OVERS USE THE SAME WORD. Your refrain 'Let's see' is good structure, but the givers' lines repeat the word 'list': Nani 'My lane, your list.', Mummy 'The list is yours.', Mami 'You run my list.' (Papa's 'you're in charge' and Tinku's 'your call' differ). Five relays with the same noun read as one beat repeated. Fix: 'list' stays Mami's word. Nani hands over in weighing words ('Meri gali. Tumhara tol.'), and Mummy with the red pen ('The pen's yours. The week too.').

TOO MANY THINGS ARE HELD OUT OR RUN OUT OF FRAME TOWARDS YOU. painter_prompt allows things 'held out at arm's length in the giver's own two hands with the giver's face in the frame'. The cast files add Papa's list (1.10), Mausa ji's half orange, Masterji's tea, Mausi's foil parcel, Captain sahab's lobbed ball, Masterji's tape 'running out of the bottom of the frame' and Mausa ji's chairs that 'leave the panel at the bottom edge'. Bible line 78 says household hands never reach towards you. Once six people do it, it stops meaning anything, and anything taut or carried that exits at the bottom edge is where the painter adds your hand. Fix: one giving gesture per person, mostly onto surfaces: Papa lays the list on the berth, Masterji sets the tumbler on the step, Mausa ji puts the half orange on the bench. Held-out hands only at the marked beats (Mummy 1.05, Mami 5.04, Mausi's berth chart per the bible), and nothing taut leaves the frame.

LUGDI'S STYLE BREAKS YOUR EYE-LEVEL RULE. painter_avoid: 'A camera angle steeply up or down at the speaker, which would give you a height'. STYLE['lugdi'] in cutscenes.py ends 'dramatic angle', and chapter 1 is Lugdi. Fix: in every Lugdi panel with a speaker facing you, add the eye-level presence line after STYLE so it wins, or take 'dramatic angle' out of the story panels' Lugdi string.

cast_wide: THE CAST WAS WRITTEN IN PARALLEL, AND THE FILES DUPLICATE EACH OTHER'S QUIRKS. Refuses reading glasses and holds things at arm's length: Mummy, Mausi, Mausa ji, Mama ji, Captain sahab, Mami (six). Phone font at its largest: Nani, Papa, Mausi, Mausa ji, Masterji, Captain sahab (six). Sits on the front edge and never leans back: Nani, Mummy, Papa, Mama ji, Mausi, Mausa ji, Captain sahab, Mami (eight). Taps twice: Papa, Mausa ji, Tinku. Ears that stand out: Papa, Mausa ji, Masterji. Tooth gap: Mausi, Tinku. Sleeveless V-neck sweater over a light shirt in winter: Papa, Mausa ji, Masterji. Thumbs-up as the only emoji: Mummy, Mausa ji. 'Pakka': Mama ji, Mummy, Mausi, Mausa ji, Masterji. 'Suno': Mausi, Mummy, Tinku. Number before the noun: Papa, Tinku, Mama ji. Fix: build one trait table (row per trait, one owner each) from the files, and strike every duplicate before anyone paints or writes panels.

THE VOICE TEST FAILS WHERE THE CAST SHARES ONE AXIS. Seven of the eleven are defined by numbers or clocks. Papa speaks in minutes, Mummy in hours and prices, Nani in hours and head-counts, Captain sahab in rounded hours, Masterji is always 'five minutes' late, Mami numbers her items with ordinals, Tinku keeps scores, and Mama ji adds ten. Papa's and Mami's files even use the same measure ('Three of every four of his/her lines carry a figure/ordinal'). Cover the names and 'Sixteen people, twelve berths.' (Papa), 'Fourteen people, ten berths.' (Nani), 'Ten to pick from.' (Tinku) and 'Toss in ten minutes.' (Captain sahab) cannot be sorted. Fix: at most one numeric voice per chapter's speaking pair. Give Mummy, Papa and Mami one interest seen on the page that is not a number. Run a blind sort: shuffle each chapter's lines without tags and have a reader sort them by speaker.

THE SAME FEELING REGISTER EVERYWHERE. Seven elders never say sorry or thank you and swap in a deed: Nani (tea), Mummy ('Hisaab saaf'), Papa (a berth), Mausi (food), Mausa ji (half an orange), Masterji (re-measuring), Captain sahab ('Next ball'). Eight of the ten painted people get quieter when cross: Nani, Mummy, Papa, Mama ji, Tinku, Mausa ji, Captain sahab, Mami. Only Mausi (and Masterji, at things) gets louder. Rule 35's one shout per chapter pushed every writer the same way. The result is a family of stoics who all love in the same coded way, so no one stands out by feeling. Fix: give two people an overt register. Mausi says her hurt out loud ('Amma rings Chhoti first!'). Mama ji says 'I missed you' and hugs everyone. Differentiate anger by rhythm and body, not volume, so no two people in one chapter share an anger tell.

EIGHT OF ELEVEN VOICES ARE CLIPPED TO TWO TO SEVEN WORDS. Nani, Mummy, Papa, Tinku, Mausa ji, Captain sahab, Mami and You all sit in short lines, most without verbs. Only Mausi, Mama ji and Masterji run long. When every line is a three-word fragment, voices are told apart only by trade nouns (grocery, shop, railway, cricket, billing), which is the thinnest kind of voice. Fix: give each a sentence shape as well as a vocabulary. Nani: one-word fragments, each closed. Papa: whole sentences that keep their verbs. Mummy: lists. Captain sahab: calls. Tinku: questions with 'haan?'. Mami: numbered items. Mausa ji: sentences with no subject. Mausi: a tripled word plus a question she answers herself. Mama ji: run-ons. Masterji: a verdict, then a wander.

THE SILHOUETTE TEST IN EACH LOOK, SIMPLY PUT. LUGDI (chapter 1): Papa, Mausi, Mummy's band, Mausa ji and Nani's shawl are all written as marigold-lit light shapes over violet and indigo. Papa's and Mummy's files each claim the brightest shape in the coach, and the style string's 'dramatic angle' wipes out height, Papa's first anchor. RUKAVAT (chapter 2): two white-haired elders in shawls (Nani, Mausa ji), Mausa ji all teak, and Mummy a teak square at the ward door. STATION (chapter 3): three men with a cream top over dark trousers (Papa, Mausa ji, Masterji), with fine stripes and prints lost to coarse halftone. CRICKET (chapter 4): two reds with folded arms at the boundary (Mummy, Captain sahab), Papa's green stripes and Mausa ji's green shawl sinking into the outfield, Tinku's teal against green, and a whitewash-or-grey wall conflict. JADUGAR (chapter 5): five inks for up to nine people. Old gold is on Nani's border, Mummy's band, Mausi's border and hoops, Mama ji's check and Tinku's book. Emerald Nani sits beside teal Tinku. Indigo Mami and Papa's indigo-black jacket against an indigo night. Magenta is both Mausi's and the stage's. A moustached man with a cane-shaped umbrella reads as the magician. NOW: STYLE['now'] still fixes 'cool rainy-evening blues' for January mornings and the December album. Fix: before any master, paint (or flat-colour by hand) one strip per look with all ten people side by side as simple figures in that look's inks, and resolve collisions on the strip, not in ten files.

THE DIAGONAL ACROSS THE CHEST IS CLAIMED THREE TIMES, AND LEFT AND RIGHT CANNOT SEPARATE THEM. Mummy's dupatta, Mausa ji's shawl band and Mami's bag strap are each written as that person's signature. The proposed fix, mirror images, depends on handedness. Many other anchors do too: Mummy's watch on the LEFT and keys on the RIGHT, Papa's list LEFT, Mami's clipboard LEFT, Mama ji's umbrella LEFT and phone RIGHT, Nani's stick RIGHT, Captain sahab's ball RIGHT. The painter does not reliably keep sides, and layouts get mirrored. Fix: one diagonal in the cast (Mummy's). Treat side as a preference to check, never as what tells two people apart.

TEN HEIGHT RANKS IS FALSE PRECISION. The painter keeps relative height only between people in one frame and only at a level camera. 'A little taller' (Tinku 6 over Mummy 7) and 'a little shorter' (Mausa ji 8 under Mummy 7) will not show. The files also contradict each other: Mausi is 'half a head taller than Mummy', Mausa ji 'half a head shorter than his wife Mausi', yet 'a little shorter than Mummy'. Fix: four bands (tall: Papa, Mami, Captain sahab; middle: Mausi, Mama ji, Tinku, Mummy; short: Mausa ji, Masterji; smallest: Nani). Specify exact gaps only for pairs that share panels: Papa a head over Mummy, Mami half a head over Mama ji, Nani smallest in any frame.

HALF THE WRITTEN ANCHORS ARE TOO SMALL FOR THE STRIP. Panels are 1024 by 768 (cutscenes.py W, H). Shown at phone width, a standing figure is roughly 200 screen pixels tall (my estimate). At that size the following are a few pixels or less: Mummy's watch face, key ring and bun pen; studs; Nani's purse clasp; stick handle against umbrella handle; Tinku's eyebrow nick and tooth gap; Mausa ji's scar; Papa's thin stripes; Mama ji's fine wedding check; Nani's 'tiny' leaf print; Mami's 'small' white squares. Many files list these among the must-survive anchors. Fix: split each sheet's anchors into strip anchors (shape, hair mass, big value blocks, one hand-sized prop) and close-up details (for inserts and the face chip). Check full-figure picks only against the strip anchors.

THE FIXED LOOKS ARE TOO LONG TO HOLD TWO PEOPLE. The old take's Dadi entry in LOOKS is 23 words. The new fixed looks are 105 (Nani), 114 (Mama ji), 148 (Mummy) and 184 (Mami), by my count. At 5.03, Mama ji and Mami alone come to 298 words before scene words, the Jadugar style and STORY_NO. The more descriptive words two people share in one prompt, the more the painter swaps traits between them (the method notes' point, which the files cite). Fix: two tiers. Use the long text only to paint each master. In panels where the reference picture is supplied, use a tag of 20 to 30 words holding the four or five strip anchors. Test both on the 5.03 pair first and record the swap rate.

THE REFERENCE LIMIT CANNOT COVER THE SCENES THE FILES LOVE MOST. The files plan 'at most two people from references in a panel (klein takes four reference pictures)', and each signature prop also wants its own reference (stick, purse, key ring, list, umbrella, scorebook, basket bag, orange, tape, ball, clipboard, red pen). A two-person panel with both props fills all four slots, and Mama ji's file already found no slot left for the place. Meanwhile the best scenes listed are crowds: the night-train bay, the ward with the lane at the door, the front row, the cake at 5.28 and the album. No file says how a third to tenth person is painted. Fix: (a) paint each master holding or wearing its signature prop, so a person and their prop take one slot; (b) add a 'far' spec to every sheet, the silhouette and two value blocks only, for when a person is small and painted from words; (c) stage crowds with two reference faces up front and the rest small, side-on or from behind; (d) treat the album as a planned group shot built in passes or as split panels.

THE PAYOFFS PILE UP AT 5.28, AND FOUR PEOPLE CLAIM ONE PROP. At the cake, Nani lets something be carried to her. Mummy lights the candle and sits back. Mami cries, gets the first slice and sits back. Mama ji is calm with an arm round Mami. Mausi's box gives the candle. The album then carries lines from Nani, Papa, Mummy, Tinku, Mausi and You. The candle box itself is Nani's ('A shut box of birthday candles sits on the stool'), Mausi's ('bought ... in January ... ridden in her basket bag ever since'), Mummy's ('kept in her cash drawer since May') and, per Mami's file, 'the box Nani has kept since May'. Fix: one owner for the box and one payoff per panel. Spread the rest across 5.25 to 5.30 and the album, and cut album lines to the two that matter (Nani's count, your reply).

THE MOST CROWDED SCENES ARE IN THE CLOTHES FURTHEST FROM THE MODEL SHEETS. The wedding night, the cake and the album are the cast's only all-together pictures, and they are in occasion dress. Several occasion outfits drop the person's pattern: Mausi plain magenta (loses the flowers), Mami plain indigo (loses the diamonds), Mama ji a fine check (reads flat), Papa self-coloured stripes (invisible). Papa and Mama ji wear the same cut, a kurta under a sleeveless stand-collar jacket. Fix: comics keep the costume. Each occasion outfit is the signature colour and pattern at the signature scale, in a finer cloth.

ROLE WORDS FOLLOW NO SINGLE POLICY. Mummy's file rejects 'the mother' because the painter may add a child, and Mausa ji's rejects 'aunt' because it may paint a second person. Yet Nani is 'the grandmother', Papa 'the father', Mausi 'the aunt' and Mama ji 'the city uncle'. 'The old cricketer' sits beside ROLE's 'the young cricketer'. Fix: one rule for all ten. Role words come from the person's look or trade, never a relation ('the tiny white-haired woman', 'the tall thin clerk', 'the copper-haired woman', 'the old man in the white sun hat'), checked against ROLE in cutscenes.py.

THE PROPOSED GLOSSARY ROWS COLLIDE. The painter-glossary rule allows one definition per word, but the files define the same word differently. 'Chappals': Nani's 'plain dark-brown slip-on sandals with one strap over the foot' against Mausi's 'each with one wide padded strap across the toes'. 'Studs': gold in Nani's row, which Mami reuses, silver on Tinku. 'Cardigan': Mummy's maroon wool against Mausi's cream hand-knit. 'Shawl': Nani's oatmeal against Mausa ji's olive. 'Stool': the existing low wooden row against Mummy's plastic one. 'Kurta' and the stand-collar jacket appear in four files. Fix: merge all rows into one glossary before any master. Use distinct nouns that carry no names ('oatmeal shawl', 'olive shawl'), or one shared definition.

OBJECT STAND-INS KEEP THE REVIEW'S BIGGEST PROBLEM. The review's problem 5: 'The strip shows a clock, not people.' Several files still carry people through things: Mausi's basket bag in chapters 2 to 5, Mama ji as a ringing phone, his umbrella in the album, Mausa ji's bulb, Nani as a pencil circle and an off-panel call, Papa 'far across the platform', Captain sahab's turn spoken off panel. One object stand-in per person is good comic shorthand; as the default it rebuilds the empty rooms. Fix: wherever the rulebook allows a silent presence, paint the person, small but face-on, and keep each object stand-in to one beat.

CONTINUITY ERRORS THAT WOULD BE PAINTED INTO THE SHEETS. Headcount: Nani's and Mausi's samples say fourteen people and ten berths, Papa's and Tinku's say sixteen and twelve, and the draft bible says fourteen. Coach: Mausa ji's 'AC coach' against the sleeper S4. Skin: Mummy's and Mausi's files still list Mama ji as 'warm light brown' after his file deepened him. Hands: bible line 78 ('Household hands never reach towards you') against Papa's 1.10 hand-over. Fix: settle each once in the cast table, and in the case of skin, on a painted swatch strip, not in words.

THE TYPE TEST, RANKED, AND WHAT TO KEEP. Readable and memorable now: Captain sahab (hat and tossed ball), Mausi (copper puff, hoops, flowers, basket bag), Masterji (bald curve, half-moons, tape), Nani (smallest figure, upright stick), and Mama ji's umbrella. Strong voice devices worth protecting: Mausa ji's sentences with no 'I', Masterji's wander, Mausi's exact memory, Mummy's politeness rising when cross. Most at risk of reading as stock: Papa (the punctual railway dad, and the first asker), Mami (the planner who cries at the unplanned thing), Mausa ji (the silent fixer uncle), Captain sahab's grudge (the gully uncle who nearly played), Tinku's headphones-and-ponytail. In each case the specific part (the colony-gate boy, the 2001 wedding-week list, the dead bulb, the 2002 match ball, the knees-up scorer's pose) lives in backstory or off panel. Fix: give each of these five one wordless panel that shows their specific past.

ORDER OF WORK FOR CONSISTENCY. Most failures above are between people, not within one person, yet every sheet's first step is a single-person master turnaround. Fix: first the line-up (all ten as black shapes at phone width, at the four height bands) and the six look strips. Then the trait-table dedupe. Then the masters with props baked in. All painting goes through heavyq one job at a time, as the files say, with the owner approving the pictured line-up before any individual sheet. Sources I opened for this review: cutscenes.py (STYLE, STYLE['now'], STORY_NO, LOOKS, ROLE, W and H), situations.md (glossary rows), the draft review saal-bhar-draft-2026-10-26.md, the rulebook (rules 7, 33, 35, 62 and question 7), and bible.md lines 28 and 78 plus its headcount. Everything else comes from the cast files as given.

per_character.name: Nani (नानी), turning 80
problems: catchphrases 'पूरा तोलो। | Poora tolo. | Full weight.': this is not a real saying. A Hindi-first reader will hear an order to weigh something. The grocer's idiom every north Indian knows is डंडी मारना (tipping the scale). FIX: 'डंडी मत मारना।' | 'Dandi mat maarna.' | 'No thumb on the scale.' It carries her 44 years at the counter and means 'do it honestly and fully'. Sunita, whose husband runs a grocery, would know it at once. If a weighing word stays, the standard spelling is तौलो, not तोलो.

samples 'मेरी गली हाज़िर। इनसे काम लो।': हाज़िर is court and roll-call Hindi. Said by a grocer to her grandchild it sounds stagey, like a film zamindar. FIX: 'पूरी गली आई है। काम पे लगाओ।' | 'Poori gali aayi hai. Kaam pe lagao.' | 'The whole lane's here. Put them to work.' It is a command, so it marks no gender.

uses 'हुक्म (order, as in डॉक्टर का हुक्म)': hukum is feudal and court register, and in Rajasthan it is how people address nobility. That is the wrong class and the wrong region for a small-town grocer. FIX: drop it. She says 'डॉक्टर ने कहा है'.

samples 'डॉक्टर बोले, एक रात। मैंने हाँ कहा।': बोले is the masculine honorific, so Nani's first line on the ward makes the doctor a man (a woman doctor would be बोलीं). Mausa ji's file plans for the doctor to keep no gender. FIX: 'डॉक्टर ने कहा, एक रात। मैंने हाँ कहा।' With ने, the verb agrees with nobody's gender.

relationships PAPA 'She teases his clock ("Does the sun rise by your watch too?")': Papa's own file gives him no wristwatch at all ('no wristwatch ... he trusts the phone's railway time'). Any reader who meets both files will catch it. FIX: 'आपके टाइमटेबल से सूरज भी उठता है?' | 'Aapke timetable se suraj bhi uthta hai?' | 'Does the sun rise by your timetable too?'

tics 'बड़ी (the eldest, Mausi), मँझली (the middle one, Mummy), छोटे (the youngest, Mama ji)': बड़ी and छोटे pass anywhere in the north. मँझली sounds rural eastern UP or Bihar, and most Hindi-first readers hear it first as मँझली बहू, the middle daughter-in-law, so Mummy may come across as a bahu. Mummy and Mausa ji also call Mama ji छोटे, so three people share one nickname. FIX: keep बड़ी and छोटे. For Mummy use no word, or a teasing shop nickname such as 'दुकानवाली'. The Hindi-first readers confirm.

address 'To PAPA, MAUSA JI and MAMI: आप ... Everyone who married into her family gets आप': आप to a son-in-law is what every north Indian mother-in-law says. आप to a daughter-in-law of 25 years is rare in a small-town home. Readers will take it either as coldness towards Mami or as a refined Lucknow-style register that pins the family to one class. FIX: keep it, but make it a trait people see. Mami notes once that Nani still says आप to her, and December's first तुम goes to Mami as well as Papa, which pays it off for women and men alike.

typing samples 'अस्सीवाँ। मई। सब आएँ।' shown as her voice typing: Hindi voice typing usually returns anusvara spellings (अस्सीवां, आएं) and adds no danda unless she taps it. FIX: keep the habit of tapping the full stop, which her file already gives her, and show the spelling the phone actually produces: 'अस्सीवां। मई। सब आएं।'. Hindi-first players see these forms every day, and a perfect textbook spelling gives away a writer's hand.

per_character.name: Mummy (मम्मी), 52
problems: backstory 'an electrical shop on the station road, facing the platform' and Papa's 'His parcel office faces her shutter across the platform': a private shop cannot face a platform. Platforms sit inside the station fence, and shops on a station road face the station building or its parcel gate. Ravi, who runs a shop himself, would trip on this. FIX: 'facing the station's parcel gate across the station road'. At nine, Papa looks out of the parcel office window across the road.

address 'To Nani: Maa | माँ' against Nani's file 'Mummy, Mausi and Mama ji say अम्मा': two files give two words. FIX: अम्मा for all three siblings. It is used across the north and the south, so Shruti and Mr Natarajan hear it as their own word too.

address 'To Mami: तुम with no address word': in a north Indian family, a husband's sister calls her brother's wife 'Bhabhi' whatever their ages, and Mausi's and Mami's files already have Mummy saying it. With no word at all she sounds cold to Mami, which works against the alliance the files want. FIX: 'Bhabhi', with तुम.

never_does 'Gives credit, until the flood week' with 'counts twice' and 'never owes': no station-road electrical shop refuses credit to the electricians and contractors who buy from it every day. Put this beside Nani's grocery, the हिसाब idiom and 'Udhaar? Kal.', and the family starts to read as the stingy trading-caste joke that the realism notes list among caricature traps. FIX: she keeps a red-ink credit book for her regular electricians and refuses credit only to strangers. 'Udhaar? Kal.' stays as the joke on the shop sign. Her flood-week turn becomes credit for the whole lane, strangers included.

nothing in the file: a woman behind an electrical counter meets wholesalers and customers who ask for the man of the shop. Without that, she reads as a wish rather than a shopkeeper Ravi or Sunita would know. FIX (writers' knowledge, one beat at most, no general statement): her stock reply when someone asks for 'malik': 'मैं ही हूँ। बोलिए।' | 'Main hi hoon. Boliye.' | 'You're looking at her. Go ahead.'

typing 'She never texts Nani. Nani gets a call, at nine' (so Mummy calls) against Nani's file 'At nine she calls Mummy' and Mummy's own sample 'माँ का फ़ोन नहीं आया': who rings whom changes between files. FIX: Nani rings and Mummy waits. That is the version 'Ten past nine. Maa hasn't called.' already needs.

posture 'She stands all day: the plastic stool behind her counter is for the hired hand': Indian shopkeepers sit, on a stool or a gaddi, so 27 years of standing will look like a writer's device. FIX: keep it, but let players see it noticed once, for example Tinku: 'Sit, Mummy. The stool won't bite.'. Otherwise Sunita and Ravi will simply find her odd.

per_character.name: Papa (पापा), 56
problems: year_arc 'he books at the minute the window opens, twelve berths' and typing '12 berths confirmed': a railway clerk and his family travel on his privilege pass, and every railway family says 'pass pe jaayenge'. One booking also holds at most six passengers, so twelve berths means two PNRs. Mr Natarajan and Ravi would expect a railway man to know both. FIX: 'Our four on my pass. Two PNRs for the rest.' | 'हम चार मेरे पास पर। बाक़ी के दो PNR।' The pass gives him one more thing to be exact about, and it makes him a real railway father.

Mummy's backstory 'Papa cooks on weekdays and she cooks on Sundays': this is believable only because her shutter comes down at 8:30, and only if nobody praises it. Shown once as a lesson, it becomes the 'one-sided message' that Ravi quits over. FIX: show the reason on screen once (he is home at six, she at nine). He makes one dish, dal, and nobody comments.

relationships TINKU 'he wants her to sit the railway's recruitment exam' against Tinku's file 'he wants her to sit the bank exams': the two files disagree. FIX: the railway exam in both. It is his world.

catchphrase/samples 'सोलह लोग, बारह बर्थ' against Nani's 'चौदह लोग, दस बर्थ' and Mausi's 'हम चौदह': a man who counts to the minute would never let the headcount drift. FIX: one count everywhere, 16 and 12, and update Nani's and Mausi's lines.
samples 'दो मिनट का स्टॉप': railway men say हॉल्ट or स्टॉपेज. FIX: 'दो मिनट का हॉल्ट। कोई नीचे न उतरे।' The trade word is his, and it is one every traveller knows.

backstory 'sends the family a good-morning flower at 6:10' with 'walks with Captain sahab at six ... say nothing for half an hour': the most exact man in the cast would not post halfway through his silent walk. FIX: 6:35, after the walk, which also suits Mr Natarajan's 6:30 coffee.

per_character.name: Mama ji (मामा जी), 47
problems: backstory 'He married Mami in the city in 2001. Nani came for the day and caught the night train home that evening, because the grocery could not stay shut' against Mami's file 'They married in 2001 at Nani's house' (her whole list habit grows from that week): the files contradict each other. Mama ji's version would also scandalise any lane: no mother misses her only son's wedding for her shop, and a new bride comes to the groom's family home. FIX: keep Mami's version and cut Nani's day trip.

samples joke 'साठ कुर्सियाँ? दस लोग खड़े-खड़े। भाषण छोटे होंगे।': a north Indian home wedding has no speeches, so a native reader hears a Western wedding. FIX: 'साठ कुर्सियाँ? दस लोग खड़े-खड़े। खाना जल्दी निपटेगा।' | 'Ten can stand. Dinner goes faster.'

samples 'इस बार अम्मा को ट्रेन नहीं लेनी।': 'ट्रेन लेना' is English 'take a train' in Hindi words. Hindi says पकड़ना. FIX: 'इस बार अम्मा ट्रेन नहीं पकड़ेंगी।' (about Nani, so the gender is hers) | 'This time Amma doesn't catch a train.'

catchphrases Hinglish 'Saath? Sattar kar do!': in Roman letters 'saath' is also 'with' or 'together', so Hinglish readers like Ravi will stumble on the year's best line. FIX: figures in Hinglish, as his typing already uses: '60? 70 kar do!'.

essence 'he worries about everything, but plans nothing' against Mami, who 'plans every minute': the worrying husband and the calm list-running wife is the sitcom swap. In a cast where every woman runs something and the men are late (Masterji), grudging (Captain sahab) or silent, Ravi, and the hostile screenshotter in the anti-personas, will read 'men are the ones to be managed'. FIX: give him one competence on screen that only he can supply. The tent man, the band and the cook turn up because his salesman's phone book and charm work, and his bigger number is right once (eight more guests do come).

per_character.name: Tinku (टिंकू), 21
problems: outfits WEDDING WEEK 'a straight teal cotton-silk kurti to the knee ... over straight mid-blue jeans': at a small-town home wedding, a 21-year-old in jeans at the main function would be sent back to change by Nani and Mummy, and it reads as the rebel-girl cliché. FIX: a teal straight kurta with black churidar or palazzo and a plain black dupatta pinned on one shoulder (the same pin Mummy uses keeps it off her head), headphones still round her neck.

voice mix 'With you: English clauses with Hindi tags, the most English in the house': the Dehradun speakers behind this note were upper middle class and English-medium (realism notes 1.1). A BCom student in a junction town talks to her sibling on a Hindi frame with English nouns. Whole English clauses at home sound metro, Shruti rather than Ravi's sister. FIX: a Hindi frame with English cricket and commerce nouns and a few English tags ('Third time, haan?' stays). Let the English come out more in her typing.

glasses_jewellery 'plain matte black over-ear headphones ... for radio commentary': in a junction town a 21-year-old wears a Bluetooth neckband earphone. Over-ear headphones read metro or gamer, and she would stream commentary on her phone, while radio is Nani's. FIX: commentary 'on her phone'. Weigh the neckband, which Ravi and Meena would know from their own streets, against the headphones' stronger outline. The painter should choose knowing this.

name 'Tinku': in much of the Hindi belt, Tinku sits with Pintu and Bunty as a boy's pet name. Until the label lands, many players will picture a boy, and some may read 'a girl with a boy's pet name who scores cricket' as the tomboy cliché. FIX: the Hindi-first readers say which way it leans. If it leans male, keep it and give it a family reason, or pick a pet name used for girls as often as for boys.
typing 'papa / 16 counted twice / b2 boarded / 0 delays so far': B2 is an AC three-tier coach, and chapter 1 travels in sleeper coach S4. FIX: 's4 boarded'.
relationships PAPA 'he wants her to sit the bank exams' against Papa's 'railway's recruitment exam': FIX: the railway exam in both files.

per_character.name: Mausi (मौसी), about 55, chapter 1 voice
problems: address 'To Papa: Tinku ke Papa, आप': naming a man by his child is how a wife names her own husband, so from Mausi it sounds as though she were his wife. Mummy's file also rejects 'Tinku ke Papa' because families name a man by the eldest child, and Tinku is the youngest. FIX: no address word and आप (she is loud enough not to need one), or whatever word the Hindi-first readers say an elder sister uses for her younger sister's husband.

samples COMFORTING 'Arre, arre, arre. Main hoon na. Aao, baitho.': 'मैं हूँ न' is a famous film title, which Mama ji's and the You files both ban under rule 3. FIX: 'अरे, अरे, अरे। आओ, मेरे पास बैठो।' | 'Arre, arre, arre. Aao, mere paas baitho.' | 'Hey, hey, hey. Come, sit by me.'
samples MOVED 'नीचे की बर्थ? मेरे लिए? किसने की?': 'किसने की' is missing its verb, and native ears hear the gap. FIX: 'नीचे की बर्थ? मेरे लिए? किसने करवाई?' | 'Kisne karwaayi?' | 'Who arranged this?'

hair and glasses_jewellery 'falling open in big loose waves ... two big plain thin gold hoop earrings': henna-red hair is exactly right for a 55-year-old in a small town. Worn open and puffed with big hoops, though, it reads as the city kitty-party aunty, the very caricature the file guards against, and Sunita's lane teacher would wear her hair tied. FIX: the same copper hair twisted up in a big plain plastic claw clip, which women of every age, region and community wear and which keeps the wide round outline, with medium plain gold hoops.
samples THE SHOUT 'दस बर्थ? हम चौदह के लिए?': this headcount is out of step with Papa's 16 and 12. FIX: 'बारह बर्थ? हम सोलह लोगों के लिए?' The added लोगों is also how people actually say it.
address 'What they call her: ... Mami "Didi"' against Mami's file 'Badi Didi': FIX: 'Badi Didi' in both, since Mummy is plain 'Didi' to Mami.

per_character.name: Mausa ji (मौसा जी), about 58, chapter 2's voice
problems: outfits EVERYDAY 'his thin, plain olive-green cotton shawl, no border, folded lengthwise into a long band over his left shoulder by day' in chapters 1 to 4 (May, July, August): in Hindi-belt heat, men of 58 carry a cotton towel (angocha or gamchha) over the shoulder, and a lineman uses it to wipe sweat. A shawl in August looks like a costume. FIX: 'a plain olive cotton towel folded over his left shoulder' with no checks (checked gamchhas lean Bihar or Bengal), and the olive wool shawl for December only.

backstory 'He retired last December at 58': as far as I know (readers to confirm; I opened no source), most Hindi-belt state boards retire staff at 60, and Mr Natarajan, a retired bank officer, knows these rules. FIX: make him 60 and retired last December, or keep 58 and say he took voluntary retirement after the 1998 burn.

samples COMFORTING 'अम्मा जी पक्की हैं।': पक्की said of a woman means shrewd or stubborn ('बड़ी पक्की है'), not tough, so the comfort comes out as a complaint. FIX: 'अम्मा जी मज़बूत हैं।' | 'Amma ji mazboot hain.' | 'Amma ji's tough.'

prop 'an orange from the bag of fruit every hospital visitor brings' (May): in much of the north the May ward fruit is mosambi or bananas, and oranges are a winter fruit (readers confirm the season). FIX: if readers say oranges are off-season, keep the act but change the fruit. He peels a banana and hands you half ('Lo. Aadha.'), or thumbs open a thick-skinned mosambi. The file's own fallback forgets that mosambi is usually cut, not peeled.

per_character.name: Masterji (मास्टरजी), about 60, chapter 3's voice
problems: address 'Mama ji: "Mama ji" (the lane's word), तुम': a ji word takes आप. 'मामा जी, तुम...' clashes, and Hindi ears will wince. FIX: either 'Mama ji' with आप, or the childhood pet name Mausi uses ('Munna') with तुम, which fits a man who measured him at twenty.

role label 'मास्टरजी, बगल वाले टेलर': the everyday north Indian phrase is 'टेलर मास्टर'. FIX: 'मास्टरजी, बग़ल वाले टेलर मास्टर' | 'Masterji, bagal wale tailor master'. It also stops readers from the east, Meena among them, hearing Masterji as a schoolteacher.

samples TEASE 'फिर नौ बजे? कीचड़ भी दस बजे खुलता है।': 'even the mud opens at ten' does not land as a joke in Hindi. FIX: 'फिर नौ बजे? ग्राहक तो दस बजे जागते हैं।' | 'Nine again? Customers wake at ten.'

glasses_jewellery 'Small half-moon reading spectacles': Indian men of 60 mostly wear full-frame bifocals from the local optician. Half-moons look like a British tailor from a picture book. FIX: plain thick rectangular frames pushed low on the nose. He can still look over the top of them, and they stay distinct from Nani's round frames.

relationships HIS OWN FAMILY 'his wife does the hand-finishing at home (buttons, buttonholes, hand hems)': Sunita is a tailor who works from home. She will notice that the woman who tailors is invisible while the man is the expert. FIX: one line in his own voice that credits her: 'काज मेरी घरवाली के हाथ के हैं।' | 'The buttonholes are my wife's.' It makes him more real and costs nothing.

per_character.name: Captain sahab (कप्तान साहब), about 65
problems: backstory cup rule 'Lives on the lane? Plays.' | 'गली में रहते हो? खेलो।': रहते हो is the masculine (or plural) form. Said to the player it fails rule 66's second check and gives the player a gender. FIX: 'गली में घर है? तो खेलो।' | 'Gali mein ghar hai? Toh khelo.' | 'Live on the lane? Then play.'

outfits 'CUP DAY AND MOST DAYS (the fixed look): a soft white cotton sun hat ... cherry-red polo ... chalk-white cotton trousers': a retired bus-depot mechanic does not wear umpire whites and a floppy cricket hat on ordinary days. That is the cricket uncle as a cartoon. FIX: the fixed look is for cup day only. On other days he wears the same red polo (or a plain shirt) over grey trousers, with the hat, so the anchors hold without the whites.

role 'Captain sahab': in much of north India, 'Captain sahab' first means a retired army man. FIX: keep the first-use label 'the lane's old cricketer' and put the ball in his hand in his first panel, so nobody pictures a soldier.

per_character.name: Mami (मामी), about 45
problems: outfits OCCASION 'no heavy gold: red is the unseen bride's', with only the small studs: at her own daughter's wedding, a bride's mother in any Indian community or region wears her best gold. Bare, she reads as being in mourning. FIX (owner's call): wedding-week jewellery that means neither marriage nor faith, such as a gold necklace set with matching earrings and a few plain gold bangles, with every neck checked close up for a black-bead chain.

relationships HER DAUGHTER 'never drawn, named ... or spoken of in a bubble beyond "my daughter"' while her one cry is at Nani's candle: every player knows the bride's mother's real moment is her daughter leaving home. A mother whose only tears are for someone else's candle will feel hollow. FIX, with no ritual: one line on her list she never ticks, 'पहला: बेटी का बैग' | 'Item 1: beti ka bag', and one silent panel where she holds the pen over it and does not write.

skin 'Warm light-medium brown ... a shade deeper than Mama ji's warm light brown': Mama ji's file has since moved him to medium brown, so Mami is now the lightest adult in the cast: the city, the money, the bride's mother. That is the colourism script Mama ji's file moved away from. FIX: make her medium brown too, or make someone in the small town the lightest.
samples TEASING Hinglish 'Tumhari ginti saath. Meri iksath.': 'saath' collides with 'with'. FIX: '60. Meri 61. Phir se gino.'

relationships HER OWN SIDE 'her mother's Bengali family ... chapter 5's circle': this side gives the cast its only strand from the east, so the card notes must keep clear of Bengali stock jokes (fish, sweets, 'babu', bossy mothers) for Meena and any Bengali player. FIX: the measure judge and a Bengali reader read chapter 5's notes for this alone.

per_character.name: You (the player, a voice only)
problems: catchphrases 'Sorted.' | 'तय।' ('खाट: तय।', 'चाबियाँ: तय।', 'मामा जी, सब तय।'): तय means 'decided' or 'fixed', so 'keys: decided' and 'all decided' do not say the job is done. Mama ji's file already gives your reply as 'मामा जी, सब सेट है।'. FIX: 'सेट' ('सब सेट है।', 'चाबियाँ: सेट।'). It is what a 25-year-old actually says, and it marks no gender.
samples 'खाट: तय। | Cots, sorted.': खाट is a string bed. Ward attendants say कॉट or फ़ोल्डिंग. FIX: 'कॉट: सेट।'

typing 'जी पापा, कोच B2, बर्थ 34। / मैंने PNR नानी को भेज दिया।': B2 is an AC coach, where 34 is a middle berth, and chapter 1 travels in sleeper S4, berths 33 to 44. Nani also never reads texts; she phones back. FIX: 'जी पापा, S4, बर्थ 34। PNR मौसी को भेज दिया।'

typing reply to 'Reached?': 'पापा, स्टेशन पर। / सब साथ।' means 'at the station', not 'we've arrived'. Papa's file keeps 'Reached' in English letters in every mode because it marks no gender. FIX: 'Reached, पापा। सब साथ।'

typing 'You reply within a minute, at any hour, to everyone' and 'you answer Papa's 6:10 good-morning flower every morning by 6:12': these turn the stand-in into one particular person. Shruti sleeps after 11 and plays on a 9 am bus, and Farida works night shifts. FIX: keep the family's view of you (everyone calls you, you always pick up) and drop the clock habits. 'Every morning' is enough.

year_arc CHAPTER 3: a whole flood week at the family shop ('Mud out by Wednesday', the Tuesday tea): players with jobs away from home (Shruti, Farida, the player's own 22 to 30 bracket) cannot have lived a week at the shop, and rule 1 asks for 'I have lived this'. FIX: one plain line that brings you home for it ('दो दिन की छुट्टी। शनिवार का शटर।' | 'Two days off. Saturday's shutter.'), or compress the beats to Friday night and Saturday.

cast_wide: Nearly everyone speaks in numbers. Papa talks in minutes, Mummy in prices, Tinku in scores, Mami in ordinals, Masterji in inches, Nani in head-counts, Mama ji in '+10' and Captain sahab in umpire's calls. Eight of ten signature voices are counting tics. Real families don't sound like one writer's device, and it makes the voices harder to tell apart, not easier. FIX: keep numbers for three people (Papa's minutes, Mummy's prices, Tinku's scores). Give Nani grocer's proverbs (डंडी मत मारना) instead of head-counts in speech, give Masterji cloth and weather without inches, give Mami readbacks without ordinals, and keep Captain sahab's calls.

Five people share one emotional key: love shown, never said. Papa books a berth, Mummy holds out a pen, Mausa ji peels an orange, Nani pours tea and Mama ji sends money. Every real family has one person who says it out loud. FIX: give Mausi plain feeling words ('बहुत याद आई।' | 'Missed you so much.', which agrees with याद and marks no gender), so the others' silence reads as character and not as the house style.

The household is entirely north Indian and Hindi-belt, and the one other strand is Mami's Bengali mother. Shruti (Kannada), Mr Natarajan (Tamil, little Hindi) and Meena (another home language) recognise the types but nothing of their own. There is no spelled accent or bobble (good), but Hindi-only payoffs such as Nani's first तुम to Papa never reach English-mode players. FIX: give one existing person a real non-Hindi strand. Papa's railway-colony childhood (several states) is the natural place: a few school years in a southern or western division, so he counts trains under his breath in that language, with a reader from there signing it off. Also give every Hindi-only beat an English-mode equivalent.

Every married woman (Mummy, Mausi, Mami) is bare: no bangles, chain, sindoor or forehead mark, the same as widowed Nani. Rule 3 makes this a deliberate neutral, but to older Hindi-belt eyes, Sunita's among them, a bare married woman of 52 reads as widowed, and at the wedding week bareness reads as mourning. FIX (owner's question): either accept it and give each woman a strong non-marital wrist or neck object (Mummy has the watch; Mausi and Mami have nothing), or allow plain thin gold bangles, which women of many communities wear, plus wedding-only gold for the wedding night, with the close-up check for black-bead chains and red at the parting.

Ten older north Indians and not one god-word between them. That clears rule 3 but leaves a visible hole: in a small Hindi-belt town, every elder reaches for one without thinking. FIX: give each elder a different non-religious exclamation so the absence doesn't show: Nani 'बाप रे', Mausi 'हाय', Mummy 'हद है', Mama ji 'ओहो', Masterji 'उफ़्फ़', Captain sahab 'अरे वाह'. No two people share one.

The greeting for an 80-year-old is missing. Touching her feet is out for good reasons, but no gesture has replaced it, so arrivals at Nani's blue gate (Mama ji in December, the night train at dawn) will feel scrubbed. FIX: a gesture families of many communities use: Nani lays her palm on Mama ji's head, and the younger ones get a hand on the shoulder. The player is never painted, so this stays between painted people.

Kin and address words disagree between files, and any Hindi-first reader will notice. The cases: Mummy says 'Maa' to Nani (Nani's file says अम्मा); Mummy uses no word for Mami (Mausi's and Mami's files say 'Bhabhi'); Mausi calls Papa 'Tinku ke Papa' (Mummy's file rejects it); Mami calls Mausi 'Didi' in Mausi's file and 'Badi Didi' in her own; Masterji says 'Mama ji' with तुम. FIX: one address table in the cast map that every file reads, checked by the Hindi-first readers and the South Indian reader (rule 65).

Facts disagree between files: the headcount (Nani and Mausi say 14 and 10, Papa, Tinku and You say 16 and 12); the coach (Tinku and You type 'B2', Papa books sleeper S4); where Mama ji and Mami married in 2001 (the city versus Nani's house); Papa's watch (Nani teases it, but he has none); Tinku's exam (railway versus bank); who makes the nine o'clock call. FIX: settle each in the cast map, then have one script grep every file for the agreed numbers and words.

Colourism by placement. After Mama ji's file moved him darker, the lightest adult is Mami: the city, the money, the bride's mother. FIX: make Mami medium brown, or make the lightest skin belong to someone in the small town, so lightness never lines up with the city or with wealth.

Read together, the trading idiom points at a caste. Nani's grocery, Mummy's shop, हिसाब, उधार, 'counts twice', 'never owes' and Tinku's accounts can make the household read as the stingy trading-caste stereotype (the realism notes' greedy-trader trap), even though no file intends it.
